rounds.text: Nam Securities Ltd offers a pristine balance sheet characterized by a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.00x, making the company almost entirely debt-free [E37, E48]. The business is demonstrating powerful operational acceleration supported by recent screening metrics, including a trailing twelve-month sales growth of 15% and a stellar 3-year compounded profit growth of 54% [E17, E20]. Furthermore, recent performance highlights robust momentum with year-over-year sales surging by 117% alongside a net profit expansion of 25% [E56, E58]. The company boasts a solid 10-year compounded sales growth rate of 38% while maintaining strong promoter commitment with a stable 75.00% holding [E14, E40]. Conceded: the valuation and return metrics present significant hurdles, as evidenced by a low return on equity of 1.0%, a negative operating cash flow of Rs -0.53 Cr, and a lofty price-to-earnings ratio of 275 [E1, E13, E35].

Nam Securities Ltd carries an extreme valuation disconnect, trading at a price-to-earnings multiple of 275x [E1] or 278.48x against a sector benchmark of just 18.76x [E6], alongside an EV/EBITDA of 126.14x [E11]. This excessive pricing is wholly detached from weak fundamental returns, evidenced by a dismal return on equity of 1.0% [E13] and an ROCE of 1.6% [E12], both severely lagging sector benchmarks [E9, E10]. Compounded sales growth has contracted over both 5-year (-14%) and 3-year (-18%) horizons [E15, E16], and the business is actively cash-destructive, posting a negative operating cash flow of Rs -0.53 Cr and negative free cash flow of Rs -0.17 Cr for March 2026 [E35, E36]. Consequently, a discounted cash flow model values the intrinsic worth at Rs 4 per share against a market price of Rs 91.9, producing a staggering negative margin of safety of -2380.0% [E42, E43]. Expectations are running unsustainably ahead of delivery, with a reverse DCF implying that the current price requires a 45.7% earnings growth rate [E44, E46]. conceded: [E14, E20, E56, E58]

Conceded: [E1, E6, E11, E12, E13, E35, E36, E42, E43, E44]. While the headline valuation multiples and negative cash flows for March 2026 are high, the bear overlooks powerful momentum in the core financials, specifically a 10-year compounded sales growth of 38% [E14] and a TTM sales growth recovery of 15% [E17]. Furthermore, the bear's dismissal of profitability ignores a robust 3-year compounded profit growth of 54% [E20] and a recent net profit increase of 25% YoY [E58]. The company's results score sits at a stellar 98 out of 100 with accelerating performance, meaning stale valuation metrics ignore a genuine operational turnaround [E63]. Additionally, the business remains completely debt-free with a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.00x [E37], and promoters maintain high, unwavering confidence with a 75.00% holding [E40].

Conceded: [E14, E20, E40]. The bull's reliance on 10-year sales growth of 38% [E14] masks a severe structural deterioration over medium-term horizons, evidenced by 5-year and 3-year compounded sales contractions of -14% [E15] and -18% [E16] respectively. While 3-year profit growth looks impressive at 54% [E20], it follows a long-term decay where 10-year profit growth stands at -2% [E18] and trailing twelve-month profit growth plunged by -25% [E21]. The touted 25% YoY net profit increase [E58] occurs against a backdrop of negative operating cash flow of Rs -0.53 Cr and negative free cash flow of Rs -0.17 Cr in March 2026 [E35, E36], demonstrating that headline profit growth fails to convert into actual cash. Furthermore, pointing to a results score or operational turnaround [E63] ignores the reality that return metrics are anemic, with a 3-year median ROE of just 2% [E28] and an ROCE of 1.6% [E12] that lags far behind the sector benchmark of 6.1% [E67]. Promoter holding remaining at 75.00% [E40] provides no operational insulation against a reverse DCF requirement of 45.7% future earnings growth [E44] when the company's own historical profit trajectory is negative [-2% over 10 years, E18].
